exercise.name: Stability Ball Back Extension
steps: Lie face down with your hips on the ball and toes on the floor.
Put your hands by your ears and let your chest curl over the ball.
Lift your chest until your body is straight, then lower slowly.
exercise.one_line_summary: Face down with the hips on a 60 cm ball, legs straight back to the toes, hands by the ears. Start chest curled down over the ball; end chest lifted until the body is one straight line. Lower back is the target; glutes help.

setup.target: Front of the hips on top of the ball, toes on the floor, legs wide.

movement.start: curled over the ball (pelvis 68 + spine 50 deg)
movement.tolerance: end in line with the legs +-10

muscles.emg: Back extensions give the highest ES (~63% MVIC floor, ~56% bench) (S1); unstable superman most erector activity (S2).
muscles.surface: The two ropes either side of the spine in the low back.

muscles.emg: Back extension variants share work with the gluteus maximus (S3).

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Chest thrown past the straight line, head cranked back.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Library step 3 stops at a straight body.

sources.citation: Oliva-Lozano JM, Muyor JM. 2020. Core muscle activity during physical fitness exercises: a systematic review. Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(12):4306. doi:10.3390/ijerph17124306
sources.what_it_gave: Erector spinae highest in back extensions (~63% MVIC on the floor, ~56% on a bench); V-sits ~80% MVIC rectus abdominis; adding a stability ball raises core EMG; sit-ups and curl-ups the classic core exercises.

sources.citation: Atalay ES, Turker D, Soylu C, Sahan TY, Un Yildirim N. 2025. Association between lumbar lordosis, thoracic kyphosis, and muscle activations during different lower back exercises. Medicina (Kaunas) 61(6):986. doi:10.3390/medicina61060986
sources.what_it_gave: Of three lower-back exercises, the unstable superman produced the most thoracolumbar erector activity.

sources.citation: Yoo WG. 2015. Comparison of the isolated contraction ratios of the hip extensors and erector spinae muscles of the lumbar region and thoracic muscles during different back extension exercises. J Phys Ther Sci 27(2):315-316. doi:10.1589/jpts.27.315
sources.what_it_gave: Back extension variants share the work between the lumbar and thoracic erector spinae and the gluteus maximus; the variant decides which leads.
